title: Build the mutation journal and kondo trash
why: ADR-0001 makes every mutation reversible, and nothing in the app writes yet. The journal and trash have to exist before the first toggle, not alongside it.
what: Append-before-write journal at <kondo-data>/journal.jsonl, a kondo-owned trash at <kondo-data>/trash/<journal-id>/, and an undo(journalId) workspace method. Ships with the ADR-0001 safety-invariant tests docs/testing.md defers to the first mutation: journal written before the store is touched, undo restores a fixture byte-for-byte, no write lands outside a known store.
notes:
2026-08-29 unverified: launch the app (npm run dev) and confirm the composition root resolves <kondo-data> to Electron userData (%APPDATA%/Kondo on Windows) rather than anything under ~/.claude. electron/main/index.ts now passes app.getPath(userData) into createLocator, and no test can construct the real Electron app, so this one line is proven only by types. Nothing is visible in the UI yet: check the resolved path, not a screen.
2026-08-29 Shipped electron/main/workspace/mutations.ts. mutate() appends one JSON line to <kondo-data>/journal.jsonl and fsyncs it before any store byte moves, then runs the move/trash/write steps; a step names a store root plus a relative path and pathWithin refuses anything that escapes. Trash displaces into <kondo-data>/trash/<journal-id>/<store>/<relative>, never an unlink; the EXDEV fallback is copy, verify, then release. undo() reverses a whole multi-step operation in reverse order, is itself journaled with an undoOf link, and moves current bytes into its own trash before restoring displaced ones. Locator gained kondoDataRoot from Electron userData with KONDO_DATA_ROOT for fixtures. Seam gained journalList, journalUndo and trashSize plus JournalEntryInfo and TrashReport; no mutation channel ships, per the plan. Red-green proof: test/mutation.test.ts failed on a missing module before the code existed, went 12/12 green after, and swapping appendJournal/act inside mutate() turned 2 of the 12 red again (the ordering case and the failed-journal-write case); the swap was reverted. Checks run: npm run typecheck exits 0; npm run lint exits 0 (oxlint 1.80.0, confirmed live by a deliberate probe file that it did flag, then deleted); npm test 55/55 across 11 files; node .jig/checks/run.mjs reports no findings. Beyond the stated file surface I also updated docs/testing.md (its safety-invariant bullet still said these tests were deferred to the first mutation), docs/plans/001 (status plus a What actually shipped table of 4 divergences), docs/plans/README.md and CHANGELOG.md, because AGENTS.md treats a PR that leaves a doc wrong as incomplete. docs/adr/ needed no change: ADR-0001 already states this design, so no ADR was invented. Work is on branch worktree-foreman-001-mutation-journal in .claude/worktrees/foreman-001-mutation-journal. Two PostToolUse jig hook firings were false positives, quoting the src/ renderer rule and the test/ real-store rule at files under electron/ and test/; the same checks through the real driver report no findings.

title: Introduce the kind registry and capability matrix
why: foundations.md names this as v0.2's structural step. A single boolean write-permission model was enough for skills alone and does not survive five entity kinds.
what: Replace the hard-coded adapter set with kinds that each supply discover, read, capabilities, enable and disable, with identity per ADR-0008. Write permission becomes a capability matrix keyed by kind, scope and operation rather than one flag. The snapshot cache, error isolation and id allow-list skeleton stay as they are.
notes:
2026-08-29 2026-08-29 Discrepancy with the brief: there was no single write-permission boolean to replace. Grepping writable/read-only/canWrite/permission/mutable across electron, shared, src and test returned only unrelated hits (`readonly` modifiers in mutations.ts and scan.ts, the string 'read-only preview' in src/app/app.tsx). SkillInfo.enabled is a state flag carried from Claude's own convention (ADR-0006), not a permission flag, and it stays as it was. The matrix is therefore introduced fresh rather than replacing a flag; nothing was removed. 2026-08-29 Shipped two new modules. electron/main/workspace/capabilities.ts holds the matrix: MATRIX is Record<EntityKind, Record<scope, Capabilities>> and capabilitiesFor(kind, scope) returns the row, with an unrecognized scope refusing both operations rather than throwing (ADR-0005). Rows encode Claude's own conventions per ADR-0006 - a user skill may be disabled and a user-disabled one enabled, a plugin-shipped skill neither, plugins toggle in any settings layer, and hooks refuse both because Claude has no per-hook disable convention. electron/main/workspace/kinds.ts holds the registry: seven entries (skill, plugin, hook, settings, project, session, desktopSession) each supplying discover, read, capabilities, enable and disable, plus createKindContext which memoizes the settings-layer and plugin-manifest reads per call. Code and desktop sessions are two entries sharing kind 'session' because they live in different stores; the matrix keys them apart by scope. enable/disable are seats returning null on every kind - the matrix says what is permitted, and no MutationPlan is built and no channel invokes one, per this entry's no-new-mutation-path rule. 2026-08-29 Invariants held. workspace.ts now names no adapter: grepping scanSkills|scanPlugins|hooksFromLayers|readSettingsLayers|desktopSessions|toSessionProjects|toSessionSummaries|summarizeTranscript across workspace.ts, ipc.ts and index.ts returns only the KondoApi method name desktopSessions, never the adapter. Every id-shape guard, badRequest and unknownId path in workspace.ts is byte-identical to before; only the line that picked an adapter changed. The lazy context preserves today's exact I/O and collector ordering - hooksList still reads only the settings layers, skillsList still reads projects then layers then the plugin manifest then the skill trees - which is why the read-path, boundary (ADR-0002) and mutation (ADR-0001) suites pass untouched. 2026-08-29 Seam: shared/contract.ts gained EntityKind, CapabilityOperation, CapabilityDecision, Capabilities and EntityIdentity, and SessionProject, SessionSummary, DesktopSession, SkillInfo, PluginInfo, HookInfo and SettingsLayerInfo now extend EntityIdentity, so every entity crosses the bridge carrying its kind and its matrix row. Each adapter stamps them where it builds the row, so the renderer never parses an id to learn what it may do. No new channel and no preload change: JournalEntryInfo.kind and MutationPlan.kind were tightened from string to EntityKind now that the vocabulary is defined. 2026-08-29 Red-green proof: flipping MATRIX skill/user/disable from ALLOW to a denial turned test/kinds.test.ts red at the 'keys permission on kind, scope and operation' assertion (1 failed, 8 passed); reverting returned it to 9/9. 2026-08-29 Checks run: npm run typecheck exits 0 (also with --force, a full rebuild); npm run lint exits 0 (oxlint 1.80.0, silent); npm test 64/64 across 12 files, up from 55/11, with every pre-existing test unchanged; node .jig/checks/run.mjs reports no findings. title: Enable and disable skills through the native convention
why: ADR-0006: kondo speaks Claude's own language rather than keeping shadow state. Disabling a skill means moving it to skills.disabled, which Claude already honours.
what: Move a user-scope skill between ~/.claude/skills and ~/.claude/skills.disabled through the journal, with the scoped equivalent for project skills. Plugin-shipped skills are read-only and the capability matrix must say so. The UI gets a toggle per skill row that re-reads the store after every mutation.
notes:
2026-08-29 unverified: run npm run dev, open the Skills tab, and look at the new toggle column. Check that a global skill shows a Disable button that flips the row to the disabled pill after one click without a manual refresh, that a plugin-shipped skill shows a greyed-out Enable whose tooltip reads the matrix reason (Plugin-shipped skills follow their plugin - toggle the plugin instead), and that a refusal renders as the red card above the table. Every one of these is proven headlessly in test/skill-toggle.test.ts; what no command can settle is how the button reads and whether the list visibly re-reads rather than flickering.
2026-08-29 Shipped kondo's first user-facing mutation. A skill toggle is one journaled move step between skills and skills.disabled in the skill's own scope; no second write path exists and nothing is unlinked. kinds.ts gained skillPlacement/skillPlan, replacing the skill entry's noPlanYet seat: the plan is built only when entity.capabilities[operation].allowed, so the matrix from 002 is the gate and a refused operation never reaches a MutationPlan. workspace.skillToggle validates the id shape and the operation, resolves the skill through kinds.skill.read, and on a null plan pushes the matrix's own reason as a new not-permitted ScanError rather than inventing prose. Seam additions: skillToggle(skillId, operation) plus its channel, ScanErrorCode not-permitted, SkillScope project-disabled. No new per-skill capability field was needed - see discrepancy 1. THREE DISCREPANCIES WITH THE BRIEF. (1) The brief asked to extend shared/contract.ts with 'the per-skill capability the renderer needs to render its toggle state'; entry 002 already ships it - SkillInfo extends EntityIdentity, which carries capabilities - so nothing was added for it and skills.tsx reads that existing field. (2) docs/plans/001 divergence 3 states project roots arrive with entry 005, and mutations.ts indeed knew only user and desktop. 003 cannot toggle a project skill without one, so createMutations gained an optional extraRoot resolver and resolveIn/rootOf became async; createWorkspace supplies project:<dirName> from its verified-project cache, resolving to <project>/.claude so ADR-0002 confinement is the store boundary itself. The ADR-0001 decision-6 containment check is applied to dynamically resolved roots too. (3) scanSkills had no project-disabled scope, so disabling a project skill would have made it vanish from the list with no way to re-enable it. Added the scope to SkillScope, a matrix row, and a scan of <project>/.claude/skills.disabled. RED-GREEN PROOF, three separate runs, each reverted: swapping appendJournal and act inside mutate() turned 'appends the journal entry before the skill directory moves' red (expected 4 to be less than 0); flipping MATRIX skill/plugin from neither(PLUGIN_OWNED) to ALLOW turned the plugin-refusal test red; misrouting skillPlacement's project case to the user store turned both project-scope tests red. CHECKS RUN: npm run typecheck exits 0 (also npx tsc -b --force, a full rebuild); npm run lint exits 0 (oxlint, silent); npm test 73/73 across 13 files, up from 64/12, every pre-existing test passing unchanged; node .jig/checks/run.mjs reports no findings. test/skill-toggle.test.ts holds 9 cases: user disable lands in skills.disabled and nowhere else with an empty trash, user enable, undo restores the tree byte-for-byte, a project skill toggles both ways inside its own .claude while the user store's hash is unchanged, a write-boundary sweep over the project toggle, the plugin refusal in both directions with no journal entry, the already-enabled refusal, journal-before-move ordering, and refusals for a free-form path, an unknown id and an unknown operation. Both project cases ran (tmpdir has no hyphen); they self-skip on a hyphenated tmpdir like boundary.test.ts. hashTree, exists and recordWrites moved from test/mutation.test.ts into test/helpers.ts so both suites share one write-path probe; mutation.test.ts's 12 cases are otherwise untouched. No docs/plans/ file was written - docs/plans/README.md says a plan is a feature's first commit, not a document written afterwards. title: Enable and disable plugins per scope
why: A plugin's enabled state lives in enabledPlugins in a settings layer, and today kondo only reports which layers list it. Toggling by hand means editing JSON in the right file.
what: Edit enabledPlugins in the chosen settings layer through the journal, preserving formatting and unrelated keys. The plugins view gains a per-scope toggle showing which layer wins. A layer that does not exist yet is created only on explicit confirmation.
notes:
2026-08-29 unverified: run npm run dev, open the Plugins tab and look at the new Enabled in column. Each plugin row now carries one button per settings layer reading e.g. "global on", "project off", "local —", and the layer that wins is ringed in the accent colour with a ★. Check that clicking a button flips that one layer without a manual refresh, that a plugin no layer mentions still shows the "nowhere" pill, and that clicking a layer whose file does not exist raises the card asking to create it with a Create it / Cancel pair rather than writing anything. Every one of these is proven headlessly in test/plugin-toggle.test.ts (16 cases); what no command can settle is how a row reads when a machine has many verified projects, since project and local buttons then repeat with only their tooltip to tell them apart.
2026-08-29 2026-08-29 DISCREPANCY WITH THE BRIEF. The handoff listed enabledPlugins as "Unresolved in the entry’s own description (not found in any touched file) - an invented API or an un-caught rename". It is neither: user-store.ts already read it in pluginEnabledIn, ADR-0006 names it, and ~/.claude/settings.json on this machine holds it as an object keyed by <plugin>@<marketplace> with boolean values, both true and an explicit false observed. Nothing was invented to make the prompt true. 2026-08-29 SHIPPED. The toggle is one journaled write step whose content is the settings file spliced, never reserialized: user-store.ts gained a ~120-line JSON span scanner (skipWs / scanString / scanValue / readObject / insertMember) and editEnabledPlugins(source, key, enabled), which replaces exactly the span holding the plugin’s value, or inserts a new member led by the whitespace the file already puts before its first member - so the file’s own indentation is copied rather than imposed. Everything outside that span is byte-identical, which the tests assert as string equality against the original text, not as a parsed comparison. Array-form enabledPlugins and a non-object root return null and the caller refuses rather than reformatting (ADR-0005). SettingsLayer now carries source (the bytes as read), store and relative, so one read feeds both the parse and the splice and no step ever carries an absolute path. pluginStateIn returns boolean | null - a layer that says nothing cannot win over one that does - and scanPlugins builds PluginScopeState per layer in precedence order (local > project > user, domain.md) plus winningLayerId. kinds.ts gained pluginTogglePlan: the entity-level enable/disable seats stay empty for plugin on purpose, because a plugin’s state is a key in a layer rather than a property of the plugin, so the seat has no target to name; that is documented on the kind. The matrix from 002 is still the gate and it is keyed on the layer the write lands in, not on the install scope. workspace.pluginToggle builds one KindContext for both the entity read and the plan, so the plan sees exactly the bytes the entity was built from. 2026-08-29 CONFIRMATION GATE. A layer whose file does not exist refuses with the new needs-confirmation ScanErrorCode and writes nothing; the renderer raises a card naming the path and only a Create it click repeats the call with createLayer true, producing a file holding just that one key. Undo removes it again (proven). 2026-08-29 BUG FOUND AND FIXED OUTSIDE THE STATED SURFACE: electron/main/workspace/mutations.ts. trashPath used the store name verbatim as a path segment, and a project store is named project:<dirName>. On Windows no path segment may hold a colon, so mkdir failed with ENOENT and three tests went red - every project-scope settings edit was unwritable and its undo unrestorable. Entry 003 never hit it because a skill toggle is a move step, which displaces nothing into the trash. Fixed at the root, in trashPath itself, so the write and its undo cannot disagree. This is real work beyond the entry’s file surface and is flagged as such. 2026-08-29 RED-GREEN PROOF, four probes, each reverted: swapping LAYER_RANK local and user turned both precedence tests red; swapping appendJournal and act inside mutate() turned the journal-ordering test red; inverting the createLayer gate turned five tests red including the two confirmation cases; replacing insertMember’s copied lead with a hard-coded newline-plus-two-spaces turned the two insertion tests red. title: Move a skill between scopes and projects
why: Skills accumulate in the wrong scope and moving one by hand means copying a directory and hoping nothing referenced the old path. This is the feature the tool is named for.
what: Copy, verify, then trash the source, all journaled as one reversible operation. Handles user to project, project to user, and project to project. Refuses a move whose destination already holds that skill name rather than merging, and refuses plugin-owned sources outright.
notes:
2026-08-29 unverified: run npm run dev, open the Skills tab, and look at the new Move to column between Location and the toggle button. Check that the select lists global (~/.claude) plus one entry per project whose path was reconstructed, that picking one moves the row to its new scope after a single click with no manual refresh, that a plugin-shipped skill shows the select greyed out with the matrix reason as its tooltip (Plugin-shipped skills follow their plugin - toggle the plugin instead), and that picking the scope the skill is already in renders the red refusal card above the table reading is already in that scope. Every one of these is proven headlessly in test/skill-move.test.ts; what no command can settle is whether a dropdown is the right affordance here and whether the project paths are readable at that width - they are full absolute paths, which can be long.
2026-08-29 2026-08-29 Shipped the move as one journaled operation whose step order IS the invariant. mutations.ts gained a cross-store `copy` PlannedStep — {store, from, toStore, to} — and skillMovePlan emits exactly two steps, copy then trash, so `undo` reverses the pair or neither. Verification is a real proof, not an existence check: digestTree() sha256s a tree's sorted relative names plus every file's bytes, and verifyCopy() compares source to destination before runSteps is allowed to reach the trash step. A copy that does not verify is relocated into that entry's own trash (never unlinked) and the step throws a Refused, so the source is never released. mutate()'s act-phase catch now honours Refused so that reason reaches the seam instead of a generic read-failed. undo() reverses a copy by displacing the destination into the undo's own trash, guarded by exists() so a failed copy does not break the undo; dropCreated is keyed on createdIn(step) because a copy's created directories live under toStore, not store. relocate()'s EXDEV fallback was upgraded from `exists(to)` to the same verifyCopy — that path is not hypothetical here, a D: project store and a C: <kondo-data> hit it on every project-skill trash. SEAM: CapabilityOperation gained a third member, `move`, so the matrix answers it separately (a `user` skill denies enable yet is perfectly movable — reusing the toggle rows would have been wrong reasoning). ToggleOperation = enable|disable was extracted so skillToggle/pluginToggle cannot be handed `move` at the type level. New method skillMove(skillId, destinationId) + channel kondo:skill-move; destinationId is `user` or a project:code:<dirName> id from a previous scan, never a path (ADR-0008). MATRIX: skill rows user/user-disabled/project/project-disabled get move:ALLOW, skill/plugin becomes none(PLUGIN_OWNED) so the plugin refusal carries its own reason for all three operations, and every other kind denies move with ONLY_SKILLS_MOVE. DECISIONS BEYOND THE BRIEF, both stated rather than assumed: (1) the collision check counts BOTH of the destination scope's directories — a name sitting in its skills.disabled is the same name arriving twice — implemented by reusing skillPlacement over the single scan the workspace already holds, with planSteps' own destination-exists check as the fs-level backstop; (2) the move preserves enabled state, so a benched skill lands in the destination's skills.disabled and stays benched (ADR-0006 — the store is the state). RED-GREEN PROOF, three separate sabotages, each reverted and re-run green: stubbing verifyCopy to always pass turned the failed-verification test red (expected data toBeNull); swapping the plan's copy and trash steps turned 7 of 11 red with read-failed on every direction; flipping MATRIX skill/plugin move to ALLOW turned the plugin refusal red (the message fell through to skillPlacement's own refusal, confirming the matrix is the gate rather than a second guard). CHECKS RUN: npm run typecheck exits 0; npm run lint exits 0 (oxlint, silent); npm test 101/101 across 15 files, up from 90/14, every pre-existing test passing unchanged; npm run guards reports No findings. test/skill-move.test.ts holds 11 cases: all three directions, the enabled-state-preserving move, the name collision in skills and again in skills.disabled, the plugin-owned refusal, already-in-that-scope plus unknown-destination plus a free-form path as destination, journal-before-destination ordering, the unverified copy leaving the source byte-for-byte and no half-copy behind, and undo restoring the source AND removing the copy with both trees hashed. Two fixture projects were added so project-to-project is a real direction; those cases self-skip on a hyphenated tmpdir, and they ran here. title: A failed mutation leaves a journal entry whose undo throws
why: mutate() appends the journal entry before any step runs (ADR-0001 decision 5 - an unjournaled write is an un-undoable one), so a step that fails mid-operation leaves an entry on disk describing work that did not happen. journalList shows it as a completed operation, and journalUndo on it throws: undo of a trash step unconditionally relocates from trashPath(original.id, ...), which was never written. Observed while adding the verified copy step in 005 - a move whose copy fails verification is exactly this shape. Entry 007 puts undo in front of users, which turns a throw into something they will hit.
what: Decide and implement what the journal records about a partially-run operation. Options seen from 005: record which steps actually ran (a second append is not allowed - the file is append-only per the 001 lesson, so this likely means the entry carries per-step outcome only via a following compensating entry), or make undo tolerant per step - skip a trash restore whose trash directory is absent while the source is present, and skip a move whose destination is absent. mutations.ts act() already guards the copy and write reversals with exists(); the trash reversal is the one that does not. Whatever is chosen, journalList must stop presenting a failed operation as a done one.
